front: What is PM2 ecosystem file in one sentence?
back: Declarative process config — cluster mode, env injection, logs, and restart policy for Node apps.

front: Explain the mental model of PM2 ecosystem file (how the system thinks).
back: PM2 reads ecosystem.config.js (or .cjs/JSON) and starts one or more apps. Each app has script, instances, env, and restart rules. PM2 keeps processes alive, aggregates logs, and supports zero-downtime reload for cluster mode.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for PM2 ecosystem file?
back: ecosystem.config.js → pm2 start → PM2 daemon → app workers

front: Given a broken PM2 ecosystem file setup, what is your first validation command?
back: ecosystem.config.js → pm2 start → PM2 daemon → app workers

front: Symptom: App not picking env — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong --env · Fix: pm2 start --env production

front: Symptom: Restarts loop — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: pm2 logs · Fix: Fix crash; raise memory if OOM

front: Symptom: npm start overhead — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Script path · Fix: Point script at compiled JS

front: Symptom: Cluster sticky sessions — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Single instance or Redis adapter · Fix: Scale Socket.IO with adapter

front: Symptom: Lost on reboot — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: pm2 save + startup · Fix: Re-run pm2 startup after PM2 upgrade

front: Gotcha with PM2 ecosystem file: what silently fails?
back: Secrets in ecosystem file — use env from host/secret manager, not committed values. instances: max on CPU-bound — can thrash; profile first. PM2 + Docker — usually one process per container; PM2 inside container is redundant unless legacy.

front: When should you NOT use PM2 ecosystem file?
back: Don't use PM2 inside Kubernetes — use Deployments + probes. Don't cluster non-HTTP workers (queue consumers) without idempotency — use fixed instance count.

front: Design a minimal correct PM2 ecosystem file setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: ecosystem.config.js → pm2 start → PM2 daemon → app workers
pm2 runs as a non-root user (e.g., ubuntu, deploy, or your app user).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for pm2?
back: pm2 start npm --name <app name> -- start → pm2 save; # synchronized with saved list. → pm2 resurrect; # restore saved processes. → pm2 show <process id>; # view the details of the process. → pm2 env <process id>; # show all environment variabel of process id.
